reason: The commit changes internal XML parsing and XML pretty-print traversal to use the existing parser-memory stack and adds an automatic compile-time indentation limit, but it does not introduce a new external entry point, input protocol, initialization requirement, or runtime configuration that the harness must supply. The existing XML and general fuzzers already exercise XML parsing and serialization through the relevant high-level APIs, so harness maintenance is not required.
evidence: tidy_xml_fuzzer sets TidyXmlOut and TidyXmlTags, then calls tidyParseString, tidyCleanAndRepair, tidyRunDiagnostics, and tidySaveBuffer, covering the changed XML parse and PPrintXMLTree paths.
tidy_general_fuzzer fuzz-controls TidyXmlOut and TidyXmlTags and invokes tidyParseFile or tidyParseString.
TY_(ParseXMLDocument) still handles StartTag input through the existing parsing flow; it changes its internal call from ParseXMLElement to ParseHTMLWithNode rather than adding a caller-facing API.
ParseXMLElement and TY_(PPrintXMLTree) replace recursive traversal with internal stack operations using TidyParserMemory.
TIDY_INDENTATION_LIMIT is a compile-time macro used internally by TY_(PPrintXMLTree); the harness needs no new configuration or state to activate the changed behavior.
recommended_action: Keep the existing harnesses unchanged; they already reach the modified XML parser and pretty-printer through supported high-level APIs.
